hook.line: A lot of trouble starts when everybody assumes something nobody checked. Spanish has a tidy way to say "we took it as settled" and "don't assume that".
hook.es: Dimos por hecho que el contrato estaba firmado.
hook.en: We took it for granted that the contract was signed.

examples.es: Dimos por hecho que el contrato estaba firmado.
examples.en: We took it for granted that the contract was signed.
Don't take it for granted. (to a friend)

examples.es: Todos dan por hecho que Tomás se va.
Doy por hecho que usted ya lo sabe.
examples.en: I assume you already know. (to a formal you)
They gave the café up for lost.

examples.es: ¿Das por hecho que Altamira va a ganar?
examples.en: Do you take it for granted that Altamira is going to win? (to a friend)

rule:
*Dar por hecho* and *dar por sentado* both mean "to take as settled" or "to assume". *Por hecho* is more common in speech; *por sentado* sounds a bit more written.

The verb is *dar* (*doy*, *das*, *dan*, *dimos*, *dieron*), then *por hecho*, then *que* and a plain sentence: *dan por hecho que Tomás se va*.

The same frame works with *perdido* (given up for lost) and *terminado* (considered finished).

Don't add *de*: it is *por hecho que*, never *de que*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *dar por* plus an adjective a resultative expression: you treat something as already being that way.

readAndPick.es: Dimos por hecho que el contrato estaba firmado.
options: They took it for granted that the contract was signed.
We took it for granted that the contract was signed.
I took it for granted that the contract was signed.

readAndPick.es: Todos dan por hecho que Tomás se va.
options: Everyone assumes Tomás is leaving.
Everyone assumed Tomás left.
Tomás assumes everyone is leaving.

readAndPick.es: Doy por hecho que usted ya lo sabe.
options: You assume I already know.
I assume I already know.
I assume you already know.
Don't take it for granted.
You don't take it for granted.
We don't take it for granted.

readAndPick.es: ¿Das por hecho que Altamira va a ganar?
options: Does Altamira take it for granted that you will win?
Do you take it for granted that Altamira is going to win?
Did you take it for granted that Altamira won?
They bought the café.
They gave the café up for lost.
They found the café.

readAndPick.es: Di por sentado que Vale venía.
options: I assumed Vale was coming.
Vale assumed I was coming.
I assume Vale is coming.

readAndPick.es: No des por hecho que el juez está de acuerdo.
options: Don't assume the judge agrees. (to a friend)
The judge doesn't assume you agree.
You don't assume the judge agrees.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *doy* or *das* and type the whole sentence: *Yo ___ por hecho que usted ya lo sabe.*
yourTurn.answer: Yo doy por hecho que usted ya lo sabe.
accept: Doy por hecho que usted ya lo sabe.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Don't take it for granted.
Type in Spanish: We took it for granted that the contract was signed.
yourTurn.answer: Dimos por hecho que el contrato estaba firmado.
accept: Dimos por sentado que el contrato estaba firmado.
yourTurn.why: *Dimos* is "we gave", here "we took as settled".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Everyone assumes Tomás is leaving.
yourTurn.answer: Todos dan por hecho que Tomás se va.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Do you take it for granted that Altamira is going to win?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Das por hecho que Altamira va a ganar?
accept: ¿Das por sentado que Altamira va a ganar?

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative, to a friend: *Das por hecho que el juez está de acuerdo.* Say: Don't assume the judge agrees.
yourTurn.answer: No des por hecho que el juez está de acuerdo.
accept: No des por sentado que el juez está de acuerdo.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I assumed Vale was coming.
yourTurn.answer: Di por sentado que Vale venía.
accept: Di por hecho que Vale venía.

pitfalls.wrong: Doy por sentado de que usted ya lo sabe.
pitfalls.right: Doy por sentado que usted ya lo sabe.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English has no *de* here, and neither does Spanish: *por sentado que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Dimos hecho que el contrato estaba firmado.
pitfalls.right: Dimos por hecho que el contrato estaba firmado.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The little word *por* is part of the phrase.
Almost. A command to a friend needs *des*, not the infinitive.

personal: Say something you used to take for granted, or something people around you assume, with *dar por hecho* or *dar por sentado*.
